safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase safety lead time from 3.0 to 3.49 days

narrative: Material PL1__M1E26DD7 shows stable, high-volume daily demand averaging 9,993 units with moderate variability (CV=0.292) across 137 working days. Lead times average 2.88 days but exhibit moderate variability (CV=0.423), creating meaningful demand-during-lead-time uncertainty. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, exposing operations to frequent stockouts; the recommended (r,Q) policy with a 20,699-unit safety stock buffer achieves 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory cost by 88.8% through EOQ-driven order sizing.
warnings: Lead time CV of 0.423 is moderate — monitor supplier reliability to prevent service level erosion
5 demand outliers were detected and winsorised at 1st/99th percentiles

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume, continuously-demanded material with stable (non-intermittent) demand and known lead time distribution suits a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. EOQ minimises total ordering and holding cost; safety stock is set via the normal approximation of demand-during-lead-time to meet the 95% service level target.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 94,088 units is not binding: safety stock (20,699) + order quantity (45,980) = 66,679 units, leaving 29.2% headroom. No capacity-driven reduction was required.
